author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Retired NASA astronaut Barry “Butch” Wilmore visited two Warwick schools Tuesday, giving Rhode Island students a firsthand account of life and work in space.

Wilmore spoke at Winman Middle School and Scott Elementary School. The retired U.S. Navy captain spent a combined 464 days in space over three missions, experience that gave students a direct connection to human spaceflight beyond textbooks and video.

Warwick Mayor Frank Picozzi welcomed Wilmore, and former local broadcaster John Loughlin helped arrange the visit, according to NBC 10 WJAR. Photos from the schools showed students gathered for the presentations and meeting the astronaut.

The visit came after Wilmore’s retirement from NASA and focused on education rather than a new mission announcement. For students, the value was the chance to ask questions of someone who has flown multiple spacecraft and lived for extended periods in orbit. School officials did not announce a continuing program tied to the appearance, making Tuesday’s sessions a special one-day event.
dek: The retired NASA astronaut and Navy captain visited Winman Middle School and Scott Elementary after completing 464 days in space.
headline: Astronaut Butch Wilmore brings space stories to Warwick schools
